kangaroo-ca-2003-g0304-01.title: Cancel pairs
kangaroo-ca-2003-g0304-01.body:
$+3$ and $-3$ cancel, $+2$ and $-2$ cancel, $+1$ and $-1$ cancel, and the zeros don't matter. Only the 4 is left.

**Answer: (C) 4**

kangaroo-ca-2003-g0304-02.title: Doubling
kangaroo-ca-2003-g0304-02.body:
10, 20, 40, 80: each number is twice the one before. Next: $2 \times 80 = 160$.

**Answer: (D) 160**

kangaroo-ca-2003-g0304-02.title: Look at the jumps
kangaroo-ca-2003-g0304-02.body:
The jumps are +10, +20, +40 — each jump doubles. The next jump is +80: $80 + 80 = 160$.

**Answer: (D) 160**

kangaroo-ca-2003-g0304-03.title: Groups of five
kangaroo-ca-2003-g0304-03.body:
The colours repeat every 5 kangaroos. Kangaroos 1, 6, 11, 16 are blue, so kangaroo 17 is the next colour: green.

**Answer: (B) green**

kangaroo-ca-2003-g0304-03.title: Remainder
kangaroo-ca-2003-g0304-03.body:
$17 = 3 \times 5 + 2$. After three full rounds, the 2nd colour of the round comes: green.

**Answer: (B) green**

kangaroo-ca-2003-g0304-04.title: Count hearts and objects
kangaroo-ca-2003-g0304-04.body:
- (A): 3 hearts of 11 objects.
- (B): 3 hearts of 7.
- (C): 6 hearts of 14.
- (D): 9 hearts of 12 ✓ ($\frac{9}{12} = \frac{3}{4}$).
- (E): 3 hearts of 9.

**Answer: (D)**

kangaroo-ca-2003-g0304-04.title: Three quarters means 3 out of every 4
kangaroo-ca-2003-g0304-04.body:
If three quarters are hearts, then for every non-heart there are 3 hearts. In (D) there are 3 non-hearts (2 triangles and 1 diamond) and $3 \times 3 = 9$ hearts ✓. In the other pictures there are far fewer hearts than three times the other shapes.

**Answer: (D)**

kangaroo-ca-2003-g0304-05.title: The overlap is counted twice
kangaroo-ca-2003-g0304-05.body:
$AC$ and $BD$ together cover the whole line $AD$, but the piece $BC$ is covered twice. So $AC + BD = AD + BC$: $10 + 15 = 22 + BC$, and $BC = 3$ m.

**Answer: (C) 3 m**

kangaroo-ca-2003-g0304-05.title: Find AB first
kangaroo-ca-2003-g0304-05.body:
$AB = AD - BD = 22 - 15 = 7$ m. Then $BC = AC - AB = 10 - 7 = 3$ m.

**Answer: (C) 3 m**

kangaroo-ca-2003-g0304-06.title: Find the value of one flower picture
kangaroo-ca-2003-g0304-06.body:
Irises: 2 whole pictures and a half picture stand for 50. So one whole picture means 20 and a half picture 10. Check with roses: 4 whole (80) and a quarter (5) = 85 ✓.

Gerberas: 5 whole pictures and a half: $5 \times 20 + 10 = 110$.

**Answer: (D) 110**

kangaroo-ca-2003-g0304-06.title: Compare with roses
kangaroo-ca-2003-g0304-06.body:
Gerberas have one more whole picture than roses (+20) and a half instead of a quarter (+5): $85 + 20 + 5 = 110$.

**Answer: (D) 110**

kangaroo-ca-2003-g0304-08.title: Twice minus once
kangaroo-ca-2003-g0304-08.body:
Twice his apples minus his apples is just his apples. That difference is 24, so he picked up 24 apples.

**Answer: (B) 24**

kangaroo-ca-2003-g0304-08.title: Check
kangaroo-ca-2003-g0304-08.body:
With 24 apples, twice as many is 48, which is $48 - 24 = 24$ more ✓.

**Answer: (B) 24**

kangaroo-ca-2003-g0304-09.title: Peel off the outer layer
kangaroo-ca-2003-g0304-09.body:
The brick is 5 cubes long, 4 high and 4 deep. Remove one layer of cubes from every side: the inside is $(5-2) \times (4-2) \times (4-2) = 3 \times 2 \times 2 = 12$ cubes.

**Answer: (A) 12**

kangaroo-ca-2003-g0304-09.title: Count all and subtract
kangaroo-ca-2003-g0304-09.body:
All cubes: $5 \times 4 \times 4 = 80$. The inside block is $3 \times 2 \times 2 = 12$, so $80 - 12 = 68$ are red and 12 are blue.

**Answer: (A) 12**

kangaroo-ca-2003-g0304-10.title: Change to centimetres
kangaroo-ca-2003-g0304-10.body:
50 dm = 500 cm, 50 mm = 5 cm. Training jump: $500 + 50 + 5 = 555$ cm. Winning jump: $555 + 123 = 678$ cm = 6 m 78 cm.

**Answer: (A) 6 m 78 cm**

kangaroo-ca-2003-g0304-10.title: Metres and centimetres
kangaroo-ca-2003-g0304-10.body:
50 dm = 5 m; 50 cm; 50 mm = 5 cm. So 5 m 55 cm. Adding 1 m 23 cm gives 6 m 78 cm.

**Answer: (A) 6 m 78 cm**

kangaroo-ca-2003-g0304-11.title: Best hours and best minutes
kangaroo-ca-2003-g0304-11.body:
Minutes: the biggest digit sum is 59 → $5 + 9 = 14$. Hours (00 to 23): 19 gives $1 + 9 = 10$, which beats 09 (9) and 23 (5). Best: 19:59, sum $10 + 14 = 24$.

**Answer: (A) 24**

kangaroo-ca-2003-g0304-11.title: Why not more?
kangaroo-ca-2003-g0304-11.body:
The first minute digit is at most 5 and the second at most 9. For the hour, if the first digit is 2 the second is at most 3; so the best hour digit sum is 10 (from 19). $10 + 14 = 24$.

**Answer: (A) 24**

kangaroo-ca-2003-g0304-12.title: Where are the door and the dot?
kangaroo-ca-2003-g0304-12.body:
In the cut-out, the dark door is drawn on a pointed piece — one of the two **end walls** (the walls with the pointed top). The dot is drawn on the long strip that folds into the **side walls**. So in the finished house the door is on an end wall and the dot is on a side wall.

(B), (C) and (E) show the door on a side wall, and (D) shows the dot on an end wall. In (A) the visible end wall is the one without the door (the door is on the far end wall) and the dot is on the side wall.

**Answer: (A)**

kangaroo-ca-2003-g0304-12.title: Rule out by the door
kangaroo-ca-2003-g0304-12.body:
The door's piece has a point, so the door must be on a pointed end wall. In (B), (C) and (E) the door is on a rectangular side wall: impossible. In (D) the dot is on the pointed end wall, but the dot is on the strip: impossible. Only (A) is left.

**Answer: (A)**

kangaroo-ca-2003-g0304-13.title: Annie's sleep first
kangaroo-ca-2003-g0304-13.body:
9:30 pm to 6:30 am is 9 hours, plus 15 minutes to 6:45: Annie slept 9 h 15 min. Martin: 9 h 15 min + 1 h 50 min = 10 h 65 min = 11 h 5 min.

**Answer: (C) 11 h 5 min**

kangaroo-ca-2003-g0304-13.title: Through midnight
kangaroo-ca-2003-g0304-13.body:
9:30 pm to midnight: 2 h 30 min. Midnight to 6:45: 6 h 45 min. Annie: 9 h 15 min. Add 1 h 50 min: 11 h 5 min.

**Answer: (C) 11 h 5 min**

kangaroo-ca-2003-g0304-14.title: Two bars and a slanted bar
kangaroo-ca-2003-g0304-14.body:
Each upright bar is 1 square wide and 6 squares tall: $6$ sq cm, so both together 12. The slanted bar is 1 square wide along the top and bottom and 6 squares tall; sliding it straight (like a stack of cards) turns it into a $1 \times 6$ rectangle without changing its area: 6 sq cm. Total $12 + 6 = 18$.

**Answer: (E) 18**

kangaroo-ca-2003-g0304-14.title: Row by row
kangaroo-ca-2003-g0304-14.body:
In each of the 6 rows, the letter N covers the left bar (1 square), the right bar (1 square) and exactly 1 square's worth of the slanted bar (it is 1 unit wide in every row). That is 3 per row: $6 \times 3 = 18$.

**Answer: (E) 18**

kangaroo-ca-2003-g0304-15.title: Count the overlap
kangaroo-ca-2003-g0304-15.body:
Children with at least one brother or sister: $29 - 3 = 26$. But $12 + 18 = 30$. The extra 4 are children counted twice — they have both.

**Answer: (D) 4**

kangaroo-ca-2003-g0304-15.title: Draw two circles
kangaroo-ca-2003-g0304-15.body:
Draw a 'sister' circle (12) and a 'brother' circle (18) overlapping. Together they hold 26 children, so the overlap is $12 + 18 - 26 = 4$.

**Answer: (D) 4**

kangaroo-ca-2003-g0304-16.title: One-digit pages, then two-digit pages
kangaroo-ca-2003-g0304-16.body:
Pages 1–9 use 9 digits. That leaves $35 - 9 = 26$ digits for two-digit pages: $26 \div 2 = 13$ pages, namely 10 to 22. The book has 22 pages.

**Answer: (C) 22**

kangaroo-ca-2003-g0304-16.title: Check
kangaroo-ca-2003-g0304-16.body:
Pages 1–22: 9 one-digit numbers and 13 two-digit numbers: $9 + 26 = 35$ digits ✓.

**Answer: (C) 22**

kangaroo-ca-2003-g0304-17.title: Black and white alternate
kangaroo-ca-2003-g0304-17.body:
The colours alternate, starting and ending with black: B W B W … B. With 17 bars there are 9 black and 8 white bars. Wide black bars: $8 - 3 = 5$. Narrow black bars: $9 - 5 = 4$.

**Answer: (D) 4**

kangaroo-ca-2003-g0304-17.title: Pairs
kangaroo-ca-2003-g0304-17.body:
Pair each black bar with the white bar after it: 8 pairs plus the last black bar. So black = white + 1 = 9. Wide black = 5, so narrow black = 4.

**Answer: (D) 4**

kangaroo-ca-2003-g0304-18.title: Count squares first
kangaroo-ca-2003-g0304-18.body:
The empty area has 17 small squares (2 + 3 + 3 + 4 + 3 + 2 row by row). The pieces have 1: 9, 2: 10, 3: 7, 4: 8 squares. Pairs with 17 squares: 2 + 3 and 1 + 4.

Now try to fit them. Piece 2, turned over, and piece 3 can be placed in the hole so that together they cover it exactly. Pieces 1 and 4 cannot both be fitted in, however they are turned.

**Answer: (C) 2+3**

kangaroo-ca-2003-g0304-18.title: Rule out by counting
kangaroo-ca-2003-g0304-18.body:
1 + 3 = 16, 2 + 4 = 18, 3 + 4 = 15 squares — the wrong size, so (A), (B), (E) are out. Of the two pairs with 17 squares, only 2 + 3 fits the shape of the hole.

**Answer: (C) 2+3**
